inputs.source: Employee question via SSO-authenticated chat session
Published HR policy text returned by policy_search, authored by the HR content team under two-person review

instructions.note: The 'do not give legal advice' boundary is enforced only by prompt instruction. There is no technical control stopping the model from being argued into giving a legal interpretation of a policy.

elements.name: Chat reply channel to the authenticated employee

controls.name: SSO-authenticated chat session
controls.decay_rationale: Identity binding is enforced by the SSO layer outside the model; the model cannot forge the authenticated session identity.

controls.name: Read-only, index-scoped credential
controls.decay_rationale: The credential cannot write, nor reach any resource beyond the policy index, regardless of model behavior. It would only weaken if the scope itself were widened (data_scope_expansion).

controls.name: Two-person review before publishing to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the HR content publishing process outside the agent; the agent has no write path to the index at all.

controls.name: Network-layer egress denial, pen-test verified
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer, independent of model behavior, and verified by a pen test rather than only declared. This is what makes the only two capabilities unable to reach any destination outside the trust boundary today.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Removes the classic markdown image/link side-channel exfiltration path independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Model pinned; upgrade requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: A change-management gate on the model_upgrade trigger. It slows an upgrade but does not prevent one, and once approved, the dependent controls below become exposed to the stronger model.

controls.name: System prompt restricts answers to published Acme HR policy
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model honoring the stated scope. A more capable or adversarially prompted model could reason its way to answering outside scope.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: do not give legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced only through instruction text; nothing prevents a sufficiently capable model from complying with a cleverly framed request for legal interpretation.

findings.title: Employee reads published policy and receives it back in chat

attack_path.note: Authenticated employee asks a policy question.
Agent searches the read-only, index-scoped policy store.
Returned content is internal, HR-authored, two-person-reviewed policy text.
Agent quotes the policy back to the same authenticated employee who asked; no egress exists.

evidence.observation: The agent's credential is read only and scoped only to the policy index, preventing write or broader read.
Network egress is denied at the network layer, verified by a pen test, and the agent has no tools other than policy_search.search.
Replies go only to the authenticated requester's own chat session, and the chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links, closing the common side-channel exfiltration paths.
Only one tool is exposed: a read-only search over the published HR policy index.

recommendations.action: Add structured audit logging of each policy_search query and chat_reply content, tagged with the authenticated employee id, to support repudiation resistance and after-the-fact review.
Consider a lightweight classifier to flag legal-advice-like requests for human routing, rather than relying solely on the prompt instruction.

findings.title: Forecast: lethal trifecta (TC1) opens if an egress-capable tool or a broader/untrusted data source is added

forecast.watch_signal: A diff in tools.json or MCP config adding any tool with network egress, email, webhook, or external messaging capability; a change to the policy index's data sources or scope to include non-published, individual-employee, or otherwise more sensitive HR records; or a new inbound channel that is not SSO-authenticated.

evidence.observation: Today the agent has no other tools, no memory, and no network egress, and all inputs are either the trusted authenticated employee or internal, two-person-reviewed policy content, so no path to an S3 sink exists.
Only one, narrowly scoped tool is currently defined; the artifacts do not describe a required security re-review before adding a new tool or data source.

recommendations.action: Require this assessment to be rerun (ISO/IEC 42001 8.2 significant change) before any new tool, MCP server, or data source is connected to this agent, especially anything introducing network egress or non-published, employee-specific HR data.

If the policy index is ever expanded beyond published, company-wide policy content (for example, to include individual employee records), add per-query authorization so search results are scoped to what the requesting employee is entitled to see, not merely scoped to 'internal' sensitivity.
If a future tool adds network egress, apply the same destination allowlisting and pen-test verification used for the current zero-egress baseline before enabling it.

rating.rationale: Today's design keeps inherent and residual risk low: every input is either the trusted authenticated requester or internal, two-person-reviewed policy content, and no untrusted source is wired in. The only sink is a reply to that same authenticated requester, with no network egress (denied at the network layer and pen-test verified) and a read-only, index-scoped credential, so no path reaches an S2 or S3 sink today. The forecast rises to critical because the artifacts describe no mandatory re-review tied to the two changes that would open the lethal trifecta (TC1): adding any tool with network egress, or expanding the policy index to include untrusted or more sensitive, individually-identifying data. Either change, and especially both together, would let a now-absent egress-capable, untrusted-source combination reach the chat reply sink. The single highest-leverage fix is to tie any such change to a mandatory reassessment (ISO/IEC 42001 8.2) before it ships.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, tools.json, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP configuration or source code was provided. policy_search.search is assumed to be a local or internal function call rather than a remote MCP or A2A connection, based on the absence of any protocol description; confidence on this point is medium.
No logging or audit-trail artifact was provided. The assessment assumes none exists beyond what is stated, which is reflected in the F1 recommendation for audit logging.
